Measures the editor process footprint.
Measures the editor view's process, layout and drag contract.
Measures HWP process, history, layout, drag and reclaim.
Measures the term view's process and frame contract.
Measures the terminal view's process and frame contract.

Checks that the official CLI upgrade of browser keeps the starter cohort (including sidecar-files and sidecar-vt-alacritty) ready.

Checks that the bytes the terminal sidecar writes to the PTY match what an independent receiver reads, which is the terminal sidecar's own contract.
Helper that prepares the default terminal surface and waits for its session. Remove it or reduce it to preparing a fake-session fixture.

Every test checks terminal behavior itself: selection, copy and paste, scrollback, scrollbar, OSC 8, mouse modes, keypad, fixture TUI, Finder drop. "dividers and card icons show their cursors..." is core (`view-drag`).
Checks that a mouse-reporting TUI drag inside the terminal survives repeated clicks.
Checks the terminal's font.family fallback and wide-glyph centering.

Checks a terminal fix (F192: the workbench sent a background open without an image). The real behavior checked is the terminal drawing shell output. A core part (a hidden tab stays mounted) could move to `plain-view`.
Helper that traces terminal input transactions for terminal-keyboard.test. Keep it with the terminal plugin, or reduce it to a fixture trace.
Checks that native keys edit and execute commands independently in three terminal shells.
Checks that a terminal opened after the earlier terminals closed displays the prompt of its shell.
Checks replay of terminal sessions with sidecar and page frame hashes stored by the terminal plugin. The core replay command could be checked with a fake sidecar fixture.
Helper that opens terminals and reads terminal screen glyphs and pixels, and is used by many core tests. It must be reduced to fixture helpers (open `plain-view`, read the fixture color or echo log).
Checks that the selection highlight follows the pointer while a status line redraws (terminal P105).
Unit tests of reconstructing the terminal's input document from terminal.screen.read and VT receipts.
Unit tests of the browser metrics benchmark case (browser readiness, history, diagnostic callbacks).
Unit test of card-panel measurement helpers. Terminal and browser are only plugin ids in synthetic data; fixture ids (`plain-view`, `extension-probe`) would replace them.
Unit tests of the editor benchmark case (editor process footprint, editor geometry).

Tests the floor-page measurement fixture and the fixture registry. It opens the floor page in the terminal card and builds on the workspace registry; it should open in a `plain-view` card from a registry of fixtures only.
Unit test of public host parity checking. Terminal and browser are only plugin ids in synthetic data; replace them with fixture ids.
Unit tests of collecting HWP startup resource evidence.
Unit tests of the HWP benchmark case (layout, marker, reclaim, footprint).
Unit test of reload phase parsing. "terminal" and "browser" are only card ids in synthetic command args; fixture ids would replace them.

Tests section-view discovery, placement, ready status and section drag with made-up `files`/`browser`/`term` manifests in temporary folders. Replace with a sections capability on a fake fixture (for example, plain-view with a declared section, a ready status enum and history).
Tests failure-evidence collection that reads `terminal.pty.pending` and `terminal.ime.trace` from the terminal plugin.
Tests how the terminal's cell screen and backgrounds are read and sampled (wrapped command output, cell rows), which is terminal screen content.

"the term view descriptor reads the statuses and commands of the term plugin" -> plugin:term; "the shell of a terminal view is the check shell of its plugin" -> plugin:terminal; "terminal view descriptor reads browser history and controls only the diagnostic frame obse…" -> core (view-drag fixture with history/frame-observer capability); "terminal source content mapping retains source interval…" -> core (capture/measurement harness, view-drag fixture); "terminal layout geometry excludes captured focus-corner colors…" -> core (view-drag fixture); "terminal geometry background uses one distinctive OSC 11 color…" -> plugin:terminal; "terminal drag layout evidence is written before frame analysis" -> core (view-drag fixture); "terminal drag geometry keeps four measured card and raster edges…" -> core (view-drag fixture with a native raster region); "terminal convergence target comes from the visible native raster region" -> core (view-drag fixture with a native raster region)

"view content reads the value that holds the shown text of each plugin" -> plugin cohort (browser/editor/hwp/term/terminal), so it should move to each plugin; "terminal content readiness preserves omitted blank cell characters" -> plugin:terminal; "view content refuses a missing, wrong or not presented value" -> core (plain-view with a content-read command); "view pixel crops include the capture content origin and scale once" -> core (capture, any fixture); "view pixel crops reject clipping and incomplete pixel storage" -> core (capture, any fixture)
Tests the B3 view-drag benchmark mechanics (native input drags, process CPU and footprint, GC_LOOP, judgment) and has no real-plugin references. It already fits the view-drag fixture.

This helper (not a test) reads the shown content of each real plugin (`browser.content.read`, `editor.read`, hwp page SVG, `term`/`terminal.screen.read`) and builds the cases for those plugins. The per-plugin readers belong to plugin:browser, plugin:editor, plugin:hwp, plugin:term and plugin:terminal; the generic harness is core and should use a plain-view content-read command.

"the surface plugins are the installed plugins whose manifest declares a surface" -> core (fake manifests, but it reads plugins/term and plugins/files and should use e2e/fixtures manifests); "the targets of a scenario come from the goals…", "the runs interleave the five applications…", "the sessions of B3 live beside the baseline record…", "the session folder holds the session and the baseline record…", "the run reads the declarations of the e2e benchmarks…", "the run conditions are read from injected readings…" -> core (measurement harness; fixture data names term/browser and should use view-drag/plain-view ids)
